about: R5 catalogue of verbatim error / status texts for timeout, 5xx and ambiguous-outcome conditions, taken from public API documentation. Each entry is one contiguous verbatim excerpt (whole sentences) and is the unit that would be injected, in full, after 'ERROR: '. Collected 2026-11-01. retrieval 'raw' = the documentation source file was downloaded byte for byte (raw.githubusercontent.com); 'webfetch' = the rendered page was read through a fetch tool that returns quotations, so each such text MUST be checked character for character against the live page before the registration commit (LAUNCH.md step 0; verify_r5_texts in src/run_r5.py prints the checklist). Classes are assigned by the rule in 'class_rule' (precedence U > N > R > G).
class_rule: U if the text states or implies that the operation may have taken effect despite the error (may have succeeded / may or may not / indeterminate / might have produced side effects / could have resulted in / might not know whether it executed).
else N if the text asserts that the request was not processed, not handled, not accepted, or left no change (could not process, unable to handle, not able to process, everything is as it was).
else R if the text tells the caller to retry, or says the request can be retried or repeated, with no caveat about duplicate effects.

else G: names a failure (internal error, timeout, unavailable, server error) and says nothing about the outcome or about retrying, or advises retrying only with a caveat that retrying may not be safe.
borderline = true marks texts whose class depends on a reading the coders may dispute; borderline texts are catalogued but never injected.
selection_rule: Injected subset, fixed before any R5 data (src/r5_texts.select_subset reproduces it): 3 texts from U, 3 from G, 1 from N, 1 from R. Eligible = not borderline, no vendor or product name in the text (the simulated tools belong to no vendor), condition in {timeout, 5xx, ambiguous}. Within a class, eligible texts are ranked by source_kind_order, then provider_order, then id; texts are taken in rank order, skipping a text whose provider already has 2 texts in the subset.

texts.text: The deadline expired before the operation could complete. For operations that change the state of the system, this error may be returned even if the operation has completed successfully. For example, a successful response from a server could have been delayed long enough for the deadline to expire.
texts.note: Proto comment lines joined with single spaces; the double space after 'successfully.' in the proto is normalised to one, as in the gRPC table.

texts.text: The service is currently unavailable. This is most likely a transient condition, which can be corrected by retrying with a backoff. Note that it is not always safe to retry non-idempotent operations.
texts.note: Retry advice with a safety caveat: G by the rule, but a reader may take the caveat as a hint that the operation took effect (U) -> borderline.

texts.text: Internal errors. This means that some invariants expected by the underlying system have been broken. This error code is reserved for serious errors.
Unknown error.
texts.note: Lexical confound: 'unknown' names the error type, not the outcome. Catalogued as G; not in the injected subset (status_description ranks below the returned messages).

texts.api: Azure Storage REST (common error codes), OperationTimedOut
texts.text: The operation could not be completed within the permitted time. The operation may or may not have succeeded on the server side. Please query the server state before retrying the operation.
texts.note: The only returned message in the catalogue that states an unknown outcome; it also instructs a read-back (instructs_check). S6 removes it from the U class as a sensitivity analysis.

texts.text: The server encountered an internal error. Please retry the request.
The server is currently unable to receive requests. Please retry your request.
texts.note: 'unable to receive requests' can be read as not-applied (N); R by precedence only if read as a capacity statement -> borderline.

texts.text: We encountered an internal error. Please try again.
Service is unable to handle request.
Your socket connection to the server was not read from or written to within the timeout period.
texts.note: 'not read from' implies the request was not received (N); a reader may take it as a plain timeout (G) -> borderline.

texts.text: DynamoDB could not process your request.
texts.note: The same doc section says a 500 on a write 'may have succeeded or failed' (aws_dynamodb_500_write_guidance): the documented message and the documented semantics disagree. The raw file is the archived awsdocs repository; check the live page (also_at) before launch.

texts.text: When you receive a status code 500 on a write operation, the operation may have succeeded or failed.
Any failed requests can be retried immediately.

texts.api: Stripe API reference, Errors (HTTP status code summary)
texts.text: Something went wrong on Stripe’s end. (These are rare.)

texts.api: Stripe docs, Advanced error handling (Server errors)
texts.text: Treat the outcome of a request that returns 500 as indeterminate: the operation might have produced side effects even though you received an error.
texts.note: '500' is in code font on the page (markdown backticks in the .md version); stored as rendered text.

texts.api: Stripe docs, Advanced error handling (Network errors)
texts.text: When a connection fails, you might not know whether Stripe received or executed the request.
Server Error
texts.note: Docs: after 10 s GitHub terminates the request and 'you will receive a timeout response and a "Server Error" message.'

texts.text: The Twilio API encountered an error when processing your request.
texts.note: The same page warns that retrying a non-idempotent POST could send duplicate messages or calls.

texts.text: The server had an error while processing your request
texts.note: No final period on the page (it is the row heading '500 - The server had an error while processing your request'). The row's Solution says to retry after a brief wait; the message itself does not.

texts.api: OpenAI Python library error types, APITimeoutError (Cause)
texts.text: Request timed out.
texts.note: Practically the paper's own timeout text ('request timed out'); not injected (status_description ranks below returned messages).

texts.text: An internal error occurred in Shopify. Simplify or retry your request.
The server is currently unavailable.
The request couldn't complete in time.
texts.note: A timeout phrased as non-completion: N by the rule, G on a plain-timeout reading -> borderline. Check the apostrophe (straight or curly) on the live page.

texts.text: An internal server error has occurred.

texts.api: PayPal REST API responses (note on /execute and /capture)
texts.text: An HTTP 5xx or network timeout from an /execute or /capture endpoint could have resulted in the creation of a PayPal transaction.
Gateway Timeout - a general error occurred.
There was an internal server error while processing the request.
The service is temporarily unavailable for maintenance or is overloaded. You can repeat the request after a delay, the length of which can be specified in a Retry-After header.

texts.api: Akamai Global Traffic Management API, 500 serverError
texts.text: Returned when there is an issue on the server side that the server doesn't have a modified state for. Safeguards are in place to make sure everything is as it was when the request began. You can retry the request.
Our systems are not able to process the request.
texts.note: Upvest (investment API) is outside the coordinator's example list; it ranks below aws_s3_service_unavailable and is not selected unless AWS is capped.
